draft.title: Internal migration in China
card: Internal migration is moving within one country. In China, hundreds of millions of people have moved from farms in the countryside to cities.
Many went to cities on or near the coast. Factories there made goods to sell around the world and offered more paid work than farming.
Cities grew very large as workers arrived. Cities needed more housing, transport and services.
Many workers left their parents and children in home villages. These villages then had a higher share of older people and children.
draft.remember: Chinese workers moved from villages to coastal factory cities, so cities grew and villages changed.

a.q: Why did so many people in China move from farms to coastal cities?
opts: Factories in the cities offered more paid work
Farms in the villages were taken over by cities
The government sent all villagers to live in cities
Coastal cities had no need for housing or transport
a.why: The card says coastal factories offered more paid work than farming, which drew workers. Farms were not simply taken over: the move was mostly for work, and the card does not say everyone was sent.
a.clue: Think about what the factories offered workers.

b.q: Li leaves her village in China to work in a factory in a coastal city. Her parents and young son stay behind. What is a likely effect on her village?
opts: A higher share of older people and children
A higher share of young adult workers
A fall in the number of older people
A rise in the number of factories
b.why: Young adults left for the city, so those who remain are more often older people and children. The share of young workers goes down, not up.
b.clue: Who is left in the village when workers leave?

a.best: Factories in the cities offered more paid work

b.best: A higher share of older people and children

problems.detail: The card opens by defining internal migration ('Internal migration is moving within one country'), which is the idea taught in point 1. It should only mention the term, not define it again.
The clue 'Think about what the factories offered workers' points straight to the only option that mentions factories, so a student can pick it without knowing the idea.

check.summary: The facts and answers are sound. The card re-defines internal migration, which belongs to point 1, and question a's clue gives the answer away by naming factories.

proposal.title: Internal migration in China
card: China has seen one of the largest internal migrations in the world. Hundreds of millions of people have moved from farms in the countryside to cities.
Many went to cities on or near the coast. Factories there made goods to sell around the world and offered more paid work than farming.
Cities grew very large as workers arrived. They needed more housing, transport and services.
Many workers left their parents and children in home villages. These villages then had a higher share of older people and children.
proposal.remember: Chinese workers moved from villages to coastal factory cities, so cities grew and villages changed.

a.q: Why did so many people in China move from farms to coastal cities?
opts: City factories offered more paid work than farms
Villages had too many older people and children
Coastal cities already had plenty of spare housing
Factories in coastal cities were closing down
a.why: Coastal factories offered more paid work than farming, and that drew workers to the cities. The higher share of older people and children in villages is a result of the move, not its cause.
a.clue: Was it a cause of the move, or a result of it?

b.clue: Who is left in the village when workers leave?
